Q: Developer python environments including DLLs A:

Your python base image defines your platform. In your Dockerfile you use COPY and RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt to install / provide what you need. You end up with a reliable mostly repeatable build assuming your DLLs don't change and your requirements.txt file is specific enough.

VSCode's remote development allows you to work in your container as if it was your host for the most part.

Q: In an XmlDocument object, how do I make sure a child node of a node list 1) exists and 2) has a value? A:

If AppendChild is used where the tag name actually exists, it will not create the duplicate or assign a value. The below code covers missing price elements, closed price elements, and price elements with a blank value.

Dim bookNodes = xmlDoc.SelectNodes("//book")
For Each book As XmlNode In bookNodes
    Dim priceNode = book("price")
    If priceNode Is Nothing Then
        Dim ele As XmlNode = xmlRequest.CreateElement("price")
        ele.InnerText = GetPrice(book.Attributes("id"))
        pkg.AppendChild(ele)
    ElseIf String.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(priceNode.InnerText) Then
        priceNode.InnerText = GetPrice(book.Attributes("id"))    
    End If
Next

Q: How use dispatchKeyEvent() in Service? A:

The dispatchKeyEvent and other key events will only work when the UI present inside the class like Activity and View classes, It will not work in Service. This because of security purposes. But you can do this using Accessibility service.

Refer the below link: https://developer.android.com/training/game-controllers/controller-input

Q: About Constrained Mixed Effects Models A:

The reason this is so hard (in both nlme::lme and lme4::lmer) is that the fixed-effect parameters are profiled out, meaning that the negative log-likelihood function we are optimizing is not an explicit function of the fixed-effect parameters (see Pinheiro and Bates 2000 for the mathy details for lme, vignette("lmer", package = "lme4") [== Bates et al. J. Stat. Software 2015] for the details of lmer). The optimization uses only the parameters that determine the random-effects covariance matrix.

It's easier to achieve this goal:

  • for GLMMs (e.g. in lme4::glmer), where the fixed-effect parameters are not profiled out (unless you use the setting nAGQ=0)
  • in glmmTMB, which uses a generic maximum likelihood engine

This document shows how to fit fixed-effect constraints on GLMMs using glmer, and attempts to do the same for LMMs (but it's not fully worked out/debugged/functional)

This question asks how to constrain a fixed-effect parameter to a fixed value
